# Behavioral Specification: USB Full-Speed Non-Buffered Protocol Engine

## 1. Overview

The module is a USB 2.0 Full-Speed device protocol engine. It operates from a 48 MHz clock and provides the low-level USB link protocol processing between a raw USB line interface and streaming endpoint interfaces.

The module:

- Recovers and decodes USB Full-Speed signaling from the line.
- Serializes and transmits USB Full-Speed signaling to the line.
- Detects and validates USB packets.
- Recognizes and processes SOF, IN, OUT, and SETUP transactions.
- Supports control, bulk, interrupt, and isochronous endpoint behavior.
- Maintains data toggle state for IN and OUT endpoints.
- Reports line status, packet errors, and transaction event indications.

The module does not buffer packet payloads. Payload bytes are presented to the system, or consumed from the system, as the packet is received or transmitted.

## 2. Configuration Requirements

The module shall be configured with a number of OUT endpoints and a number of IN endpoints. The configured numbers shall be equal. Each configured endpoint count shall be between 1 and 16.

The module shall be configured with a maximum packet size. The maximum packet size shall be between 8 and 64 bytes.

## 3. Clock and Reset Behavior

The module shall operate from the 48 MHz USB clock. All protocol timing shall be derived from this clock.

The reset input is asynchronous and active-low. When reset is asserted, the module shall:

- Return to an idle state.
- Deassert all transaction and packet activity indications.
- Not generate any USB transmit activity.
- Not respond to any USB transactions.

The module shall also accept a link reset indication, which represents a USB bus reset. On link reset, the module shall:

- Discard any partially received or partially transmitted packet.
- Cancel any active transaction and return to the idle state.
- Suppress further transaction responses until the link becomes active again.

## 4. Link Active and Device Address Behavior

The module shall respond to IN, OUT, and SETUP transactions only when the link active indication is asserted. When the link is not active, the module shall ignore transaction tokens and shall not generate handshakes.

The module shall compare the address field of received token packets to the configured device address. Only tokens addressed to the configured device address shall be considered for further processing. Tokens addressed to other devices shall be ignored.

## 5. USB Line Interface Behavior

### 5.1 Receive Interface

The module shall accept USB signaling from the D+ and D− inputs. It may also accept a single-ended differential receiver data input.

The module shall use the D+ and D− inputs to detect the single-ended zero (SE0) line state. The module shall use either the differential receiver data input or the D+/D− pair to recover the differential K and J symbols, according to the configured receiver mode.

When the differential receiver is selected, the module shall consider the K and J symbols valid only while the differential receiver ready indication is asserted. When the ready indication is deasserted, received K/J samples shall not be treated as valid protocol signaling.

When the pin-flip configuration is enabled, the logical roles of D+ and D− shall be swapped in both receive and transmit directions.

### 5.2 Transmit Interface

The module shall generate USB Full-Speed transmit signaling, including:

- SYNC field.
- Packet identifier (PID).
- Payload data.
- CRC.
- End-of-packet (EOP).

The transmit path shall apply NRZI encoding and bit stuffing.

The module shall provide transmit signaling in both supported output forms:

- A direct D+/D− representation.
- A data/SE0 representation.

The module shall assert a transmit output-enable indication while it is driving the USB line, and deassert it when it is not driving the line.

### 5.3 Oscillator Test Mode

When oscillator test mode is enabled, the module shall continuously emit a J/K test pattern on the transmit outputs. In this mode, normal packet transmission shall be suspended.

## 6. Line State and Packet Validity

### 6.1 Line State Indications

The module shall indicate when the USB line is in the idle state.

The module shall indicate when the USB line is in the J state.

These line state indications shall be updated continuously from the received line state.

### 6.2 End-of-Packet Detection

The module shall support two EOP detection modes:

- If the single-bit EOP configuration is enabled, a single SE0 bit shall be recognized as end-of-packet.
- If disabled, two SE0 bits shall be required to recognize end-of-packet.

### 6.3 Packet Error Reporting

The module shall detect and report the following receive errors:

- CRC-5 errors on token packets.
- CRC-16 errors on data packets.
- Invalid PID values.
- Bit-stuffing violations.

A packet with any of these errors shall not be treated as a valid packet for transaction processing. The error indications shall be asserted when the corresponding error is detected.

## 7. Start-of-Frame Handling

The module shall recognize received SOF packets.

The module shall provide two SOF result indications:

- A detected SOF indication, asserted when an SOF packet is received with a valid PID.
- A valid SOF indication, asserted when the SOF packet passes receiver validation, including the PID, length, bit-stuffing, and CRC-5 checks.

The module shall output the frame number carried by the received SOF packet. The frame index shall be considered trustworthy only when the valid SOF indication is asserted.

## 8. OUT and SETUP Transaction Behavior

OUT and SETUP transactions transfer data from the host to the device. The module shall process both transaction types through the same OUT endpoint interface, with a flag indicating whether the packet is a SETUP packet.

### 8.1 Token and Data Packet Processing

When a valid OUT or SETUP token is received that matches the configured device address and an enabled endpoint, the module shall prepare to receive the following data packet.

For an accepted data packet, the module shall:

- Assert a new-packet indication.
- Output the endpoint identifier to which the packet is directed.
- Output a SETUP indication when the transaction is a SETUP transaction.
- Present each received data byte together with a data-put strobe and the byte offset within the packet.

At the end of the packet, the module shall indicate whether the transaction completed successfully or was rolled back.

### 8.2 Handshake Responses

The module shall generate the appropriate USB handshake response based on endpoint configuration and packet validity:

- If the packet is valid and the endpoint can accept the data, the module shall acknowledge the packet and indicate successful completion.
- If the endpoint is stalled, the module shall respond with STALL for non-isochronous transactions.
- If the endpoint is enabled but cannot accept the data, the module shall respond with NAK for non-isochronous transactions.
- For isochronous OUT transactions, the module shall not generate a handshake.
- If the packet itself is invalid, the module shall not generate a handshake and shall indicate a rollback.

STALL responses shall take priority over NAK responses.

### 8.3 SETUP Transaction Rules

SETUP transactions shall be accepted only on endpoints configured as control endpoints. A SETUP transaction directed to a non-control endpoint shall be ignored.

SETUP transactions shall be either acknowledged or ignored. They shall not be answered with NAK or STALL.

### 8.4 Isochronous OUT Transactions

For endpoints configured as isochronous OUT endpoints, the module shall not apply normal handshake or retry behavior. The data packet shall be accepted if possible, or silently dropped if it cannot be accepted.

Control endpoint configuration shall take precedence over isochronous endpoint configuration. An endpoint configured as both control and isochronous shall behave as a control endpoint.

### 8.5 Rollback Behavior

If a received OUT or SETUP data packet is invalid, or if the transaction cannot be completed successfully, the module shall signal a rollback. A rollback means that any data already presented from the packet shall be discarded.

## 9. IN Transaction Behavior

IN transactions transfer data from the device to the host.

### 9.1 Transaction Start

When a valid IN token is received that matches the configured device address and an enabled endpoint, the module shall assert an IN transaction start indication and output the endpoint identifier for the transaction.

### 9.2 Data Transmission

If the selected IN endpoint has data to transmit, the module shall:

- Assert a new-packet indication.
- Request data bytes from the endpoint interface by outputting a byte offset and a data-get strobe.
- Accept the data byte supplied by the endpoint interface.
- Construct and transmit the USB data packet.

### 9.3 Handshake Handling

For non-isochronous IN transactions, after transmitting the data packet, the module shall wait for the host handshake.

- If the host returns ACK, the module shall indicate successful transaction completion.
- If no valid handshake is received, the module shall indicate a transaction rollback.
- If the host returns a NAK, the module shall treat the transaction as not completed and indicate the appropriate event.

If the endpoint is stalled, the module shall respond to the IN token with STALL instead of transmitting data.

If the endpoint is enabled but has no data available, the module shall respond to the IN token with NAK and indicate an IN NAK event.

An IN transaction that does not receive an ACK shall be rolled back so that the endpoint data can be retried.

### 9.4 Isochronous IN Transactions

For isochronous IN endpoints, the module shall transmit the data packet without expecting a handshake. The transaction shall be considered complete after the packet is transmitted.

If an isochronous IN endpoint has no data available, the module shall not transmit a data packet and shall indicate an IN no-data event.

### 9.5 Endpoint Data Exhaustion

If the endpoint interface indicates that no more data is available before the expected packet is complete, the module shall not report successful transaction completion and shall roll back the transaction.

## 10. Data Toggle Management

The module shall maintain a one-bit data toggle state for each OUT endpoint and each IN endpoint.

The module shall expose the current data toggle states for both OUT and IN endpoints.

The module shall allow the system to update the data toggle states using a masked write operation. A write operation shall include:

- A mask selecting which endpoint toggle bits to modify.
- A status value providing the new toggle state for the selected endpoints.

A masked write shall update only the endpoints whose mask bit is set. Endpoints whose mask bit is clear shall retain their current toggle state.

The module shall apply the USB data toggle protocol for DATA0 and DATA1 packets as part of normal IN and OUT transaction processing. A data toggle shall advance only after the appropriate successful transaction completion.

## 11. Event Indications

The module shall provide event indications for the following conditions:

- An OUT data packet was received with an incorrect data toggle, was acknowledged, and was discarded.
- An IN transaction timed out because no valid handshake was received from the host.
- An IN transaction was answered with NAK because no data was available.
- An IN transaction was attempted but no data packet was available, particularly relevant for isochronous endpoints.

These event indications shall reflect the corresponding transaction outcomes and shall be used for event counting.

## 12. Disabled Endpoint Behavior

If a received transaction is directed to an endpoint that is not enabled, the module shall ignore the transaction and shall not produce a handshake.

A disabled endpoint shall not generate:

- ACK.
- NAK.
- STALL.
- Data packet transmission.

This requirement applies to IN, OUT, and SETUP transactions.

## 13. Summary of Functional Priorities

The module shall implement the following priority behavior:

- STALL shall take priority over NAK.
- Control endpoint behavior shall take priority over isochronous behavior.
- An invalid received packet shall not be acknowledged.
- A packet that cannot be delivered to or from the endpoint interface shall not be reported as successfully completed.
- Any active transaction shall be canceled on link reset or system reset.

## 14. Non-Buffered Streaming Requirement

Because the module contains no packet buffer, all payload data shall be transferred across the endpoint interfaces while the packet is actively being received or transmitted. The endpoint interface must be able to accept or supply data at the USB data rate. If the data path cannot keep up, the module shall cancel the transaction without reporting successful completion.

# USB Full-Speed Receiver Behavioral Specification

## 1. Scope

This specification describes the behavior of the USB Full-Speed receive front-end module. The module is responsible for recovering the serial USB bit stream from the physical USB line, decoding the received data, detecting packet boundaries, validating packet integrity, and presenting decoded packet information and error status.

The module is a receiver only. It does not generate USB signaling, and it must not interfere with the transmit path.

## 2. USB Line-State Background

The module operates on the USB Full-Speed line states:

- **J**: the idle differential state.
- **K**: the non-idle differential state opposite to J.
- **SE0**: both D+ and D- are low. SE0 is used to signal end-of-packet.

The incoming data is NRZI-encoded and bit-stuffed. In NRZI, a change between J and K represents a `0` bit, and no change represents a `1` bit. Bit-stuffing inserts a `0` after six consecutive `1` bits so that the receiver can maintain clock synchronization.

## 3. Reset and Integration Behavior

The module shall be clocked from the 48 MHz USB clock.

On reset, all packet-related outputs shall return to their inactive or cleared state. The receiver shall not report packet activity, decoded packet data, or errors while reset is asserted.

When a link reset indication is asserted, the receiver shall abandon any partially received packet and reinitialize its packet decoding state. A link reset shall not be treated as a normal packet end or as a packet error.

## 4. Configuration Behavior

The module honors the following configuration inputs:

- **Pin flip**: When pin flip is enabled, the roles of D+ and D- are swapped. The polarity of the differential receiver data is inverted accordingly, so that the meaning of J and K remains the same with respect to the USB bus.

- **Differential receiver usage**:  
  - When the differential receiver is enabled, J and K symbols are recovered from the external differential receiver data input. The D+ and D- inputs are still used to detect SE0.  
  - When the differential receiver is disabled, J, K, and SE0 are all recovered directly from the D+ and D- inputs.  

- **Single-bit EOP option**:  
  - If enabled, a single SE0 bit period is sufficient to recognize end-of-packet.  
  - If disabled, two consecutive SE0 bit periods are required to recognize end-of-packet.  

The module shall also receive a receiver-valid qualification. While this qualification is deasserted, the module shall not accept or decode packet data, and any packet in progress shall be terminated.

## 5. Transmit Muting

While the transmit-enable indication is asserted, the receiver shall behave as if the line is idle. It shall not recognize a start-of-packet, shall not report idle or J status, and shall not accept incoming packet data. This prevents the receiver from interpreting locally transmitted data as received traffic.

## 6. Line-State Recovery and Transition Robustness

The module shall recover the current USB line state from its configured input sources. It must be able to distinguish J, K, and SE0.

The receiver must tolerate the brief intermediate states that can occur during differential signal transitions. A single transient sample during a transition shall not by itself be interpreted as a valid symbol or as SE0. SE0 shall be recognized only when the line actually presents the SE0 condition for the configured number of bit periods.

When SE0 is present, the differential receiver output may be indeterminate. Therefore, the line state used for SE0 detection must be taken from the D+/D- inputs, not from the differential receiver data output.

## 7. Clock Recovery and Bit Strobe

The module shall recover the USB bit timing from transitions in the incoming line state.

The bit strobe output shall provide one pulse per recovered USB bit period. The position of the strobe shall be aligned with the recovered symbol timing so that valid data bits can be sampled consistently.

After a transition, the receiver shall re-align the recovered bit phase to the incoming signal.

## 8. Packet Boundary Detection

### 8.1 Start-of-Packet

The start-of-packet output shall pulse when the line transitions from the idle J state to the K state at the beginning of the USB SYNC field.

The receiver shall not generate a start-of-packet pulse if it is already inside a packet, or if the transmit-enable indication is asserted.

After the start-of-packet transition, the receiver shall recognize the USB SYNC pattern. Only after a valid SYNC pattern has been received shall the packet be considered active and the following PID, data, and CRC fields be decoded.

### 8.2 End-of-Packet

The packet-end output shall pulse when an active packet terminates. A packet terminates when:

- An SE0 condition is detected for the configured number of bit periods.
- A bit-stuffing violation is detected inside the packet.
- A valid PRE (preamble) PID is received.
- The receiver-valid qualification is removed while a packet is in progress.

If a packet is bit-stuffed incorrectly or if the receiver-valid qualification is lost, the packet shall be terminated without being reported as valid.

## 9. NRZI Decoding and Bit-Stuff Removal

Once a packet is active, the module shall decode the NRZI bit stream from the recovered J/K line states.

The module shall remove stuffed `0` bits. A `0` bit that appears after six consecutive `1` bits is a stuffed bit and shall not be passed on as data and shall not be included in PID, data, or CRC computations.

The module shall monitor for bit-stuffing violations. If seven consecutive `1` bits are observed anywhere in the packet, a bit-stuffing violation shall be declared, the packet shall be terminated, and the bit-stuffing error output shall be asserted at packet end.

## 10. PID Decoding and Packet Classification

After the SYNC field, the module shall receive the 8-bit PID field. The PID field consists of four PID bits and four complement-check bits.

The valid-PID output shall be asserted only if the received check bits are the exact complement of the received PID bits.

The PID output shall present the four-bit PID value of the current or most recently received packet.

The module shall classify the packet by its PID type:

- **Token packets**, such as IN, OUT, SETUP, and SOF.
- **Data packets**, such as DATA0 and DATA1.
- **Handshake packets**, such as ACK, NAK, STALL, and NYET.
- **Preamble (PRE)**.

When a valid PRE PID is received, the module shall treat it as the end of the full-speed packet. Subsequent low-speed signaling shall not be decoded as part of the full-speed packet.

## 11. Token Field Decoding

For token packets, the module shall decode the token payload that follows the PID.

- For IN, OUT, and SETUP tokens, the address and endpoint outputs shall be updated with the addressed device address and endpoint number.
- For SOF tokens, the frame-number output shall be updated with the 11-bit frame number.
- For non-token packets, the token field outputs shall retain their previous values.

These decoded token fields are raw decoded fields. They may be updated before the full packet passes all validation checks. The packet-valid and CRC error outputs qualify whether the token packet is valid.

## 12. Data Byte Output

For data packets, the module shall deserialize the bit stream that follows the PID into bytes. Each time a complete byte has been assembled, the byte-valid output shall pulse and the byte shall be presented on the byte-data output.

The module shall not produce data-byte output pulses for token packets or handshake packets.

The byte stream for a data packet includes the payload bits followed by the CRC-16 field. The byte-valid pulses are generated as the bits arrive and do not by themselves guarantee that the packet passes CRC, length, or validity checks. Packet validity and CRC status are reported separately.

## 13. Packet Validation

A packet shall be reported as valid on the packet-valid output only if it satisfies all of the following applicable checks:

- The PID check bits are valid.
- No bit-stuffing violation occurred in the packet.
- The packet length after the PID is appropriate for the packet type:
  - **Token packets**: exactly 16 bits after the PID, with a valid CRC-5.
  - **Data packets**: at least 16 bits after the PID, byte-aligned, with a valid CRC-16.
  - **Handshake packets**: zero bits after the PID.

A zero-length data packet consisting only of the CRC-16 field is allowed if the CRC-16 is valid.

## 14. Error Reporting

The module shall provide the following error indications at the end of a packet:

- **PID error**: asserted if the PID check field is not valid.
- **CRC-5 error**: asserted if the packet is classified as a token packet and the CRC-5 check fails.
- **CRC-16 error**: asserted if the packet is classified as a data packet and the CRC-16 check fails.
- **Bit-stuffing error**: asserted if a bit-stuffing violation occurred in the packet.

A packet that fails any of its applicable checks shall not be reported as valid on the packet-valid output.

## 15. Line Status Outputs

The module shall provide raw recovered line-status indications for use by link-state logic.

- The idle status output shall be asserted when the most recently recovered line state is J, and shall be suppressed while the transmitter is enabled.
- The J status output shall be asserted when the recovered line state is J, provided the receiver is valid and the transmitter is not enabled. This is useful for detecting the end of resume signaling when the line returns to J.

These outputs are raw symbol-level indications and are not debounced or filtered into protocol-level suspend or idle states.

# USB Full-Speed Device Interface — Behavioral Design Specification

## 1. Overview

This module implements a USB 2.0 Full-Speed device interface. It connects to a system bus on one side and to USB physical-layer signals on the other side. The module is intended to be software-controlled: software configures endpoints, supplies packet buffers, and handles received data through control and status registers and interrupts.

The module provides the following high-level behavior:

- Full-Speed USB device operation at 12 Mb/s using a 48 MHz clock.
- Support for up to 12 endpoints, including endpoint 0.
- Support for Control, Bulk, Interrupt, and Isochronous transfers.
- Separate handling of SETUP, IN, and OUT transactions.
- A 2 KiB packet buffer divided into 32 buffers of 64 bytes each.
- Hardware-maintained data toggle state for non-Isochronous endpoints.
- Link state detection, including disconnect, reset, suspend, resume, and host-loss monitoring.
- Interrupt generation for packet events, link events, errors, and FIFO conditions.
- A start-of-frame reference output for 48 MHz clock calibration.
- Low-power suspend/resume signaling for use with an always-on wake domain.
- Diagnostic counters for exceptional USB events.
- A compile-time stub mode for systems where the USB function is not needed.

---

## 2. Clock and Reset Behavior

The module must operate correctly from a 48 MHz clock. This clock is used for USB bit timing, packet processing, register access, and internal timing reference generation.

The module must also accept an always-on clock and reset for low-power wake-related interface logic. This always-on domain is used only for capturing and communicating low-power status and control information.

On reset:

- All registers must return to their reset values.
- All endpoints must be disabled.
- No USB pullup may be presented.
- The transmitter must be disabled.
- The receiver must be disabled unless configured otherwise.
- Interrupt outputs must be deasserted.
- FIFOs must be empty.
- Any programmed device address must be cleared.

---

## 3. Configuration Modes

### 3.1 Normal Mode

In normal operation, the module performs the full USB device function described in this specification.

### 3.2 Stub Mode

The module may be configured at build time to operate as a stub. In stub mode:

- The USB datapath is disabled and held in reset.
- The packet buffer memory window must not be accessible as normal memory; accesses to that window must return an error response.
- Control and status register accesses remain available.
- USB interrupt and alert outputs must remain deasserted or in their reset state.

---

## 4. System Bus Interface

The module must provide a memory-mapped slave interface for software access. This interface is used for:

- Reading and writing control and status registers.
- Reading interrupt state and writing interrupt clears.
- Writing interrupt and alert test bits.
- Pushing buffer IDs into available-buffer FIFOs.
- Popping received-packet entries from the received-packet FIFO.
- Reading PHY status and optionally overriding PHY outputs.
- Accessing the packet buffer memory.

The module must follow the bus protocol for valid accesses. Writes to read-only fields must be ignored. Reads of write-only fields must return zero or the reset value, as appropriate.

The module must detect bus integrity errors on the register interface and report them as a fatal alert.

---

## 5. USB Device Connection and Disconnection

The module must present a Full-Speed USB device only when all of the following are true:

- Software has enabled the USB interface.
- VBUS presence is detected on the power-sense input.
- The module is not in reset.

When the device is presented, the module must assert the appropriate Full-Speed pullup:

- By default, the D+ pullup must be asserted.
- If pin flip is enabled, the D- pullup must be asserted instead.
- At most one pullup may be asserted.

When the interface is disabled, or VBUS is lost, the pullup must be deasserted, and the link must be considered disconnected.

The state of the power-sense input must be readable by software at any time, independent of override controls.

---

## 6. USB Pin Configuration

### 6.1 Pin Flip

When pin flip is enabled, the roles of D+ and D- must be swapped for transmit, receive, and pullup selection. This allows the module to be used with USB-C SBU pins or to ease PCB routing.

### 6.2 Differential Receiver Selection

The module must support two receive paths:

- Recovery of K and J symbols directly from the D+ and D- inputs.
- Recovery of K and J symbols from an external differential receiver data input.

The D+ and D- inputs must always be used to detect the single-ended zero condition.

A receiver enable output must be provided. This output must be asserted only when:

- Software has selected the differential receiver path, and
- The link is not suspended.

When the differential receiver is first enabled, received data must not be considered valid until a configured receiver wake-up time has elapsed.

### 6.3 Transmit Path Selection

The module must support two transmit encodings:

- Driving D+ and D- directly with the USB differential output values.
- Driving a transmit-data value and a separate single-ended-zero indication.

A transmit-mode output must indicate which encoding is selected.

The D+ and D- output-enable controls must be asserted whenever the module is transmitting and deasserted otherwise.

### 6.4 Software PHY Override

The module must provide register access for observing PHY pin states and for optionally overriding PHY output values.

When software override is disabled, PHY outputs must be controlled by the USB hardware.

When software override is enabled, software must be able to force:

- The D+ and D- output values,
- The transmit-data value,
- The single-ended-zero output,
- The transmit output enable,
- The receiver enable,
- The D+ pullup, and
- The D- pullup.

---

## 7. USB Link State Monitoring

The module must continuously monitor the USB line state and report the current link state in a status register.

The link states must include:

- **Disconnected**: no VBUS present, or the interface is not enabled.
- **Powered**: VBUS present and the pullup is asserted, but the link has not been reset.
- **Powered suspended**: the link is suspended before the first reset.
- **Active**: normal operation after reset and after receiving a start-of-frame packet.
- **Active, no SOF**: the link has been reset but no start-of-frame packet has been received.
- **Suspended**: the link was active and has suspended.
- **Resuming**: resume signaling is in progress.

The module must generate the following link event interrupts:

- **Disconnected**: asserted when the link enters the disconnected state.
- **Powered**: asserted when the link becomes powered.
- **Link reset**: asserted when the link is driven to single-ended zero for approximately 3 µs.
- **Link suspend**: asserted when the link remains in the idle state for more than 3 ms.
- **Link resume**: asserted when the link becomes active again after being suspended.
- **Host lost**: asserted when the link is active but no start-of-frame packet is received for 4.096 ms.

The module must clear the programmed device address when a link reset occurs.

---

## 8. Packet Buffer Memory

The module must provide a 2 KiB packet buffer for USB packet data. The buffer must be organized as 32 buffers of 64 bytes each.

Software must be able to read and write the packet buffer through a memory-mapped window. Accesses must be 32-bit word accesses; byte writes are not supported.

The packet buffer is shared with the USB hardware. The module must ensure that USB packet operations remain coherent and that software accesses do not corrupt active USB transfers.

---

## 9. FIFO Behavior

The module must implement three FIFOs for buffer management and received-packet reporting.

### 9.1 Available OUT Buffer FIFO

Software writes buffer IDs into this FIFO to provide buffers for incoming OUT packets.

The FIFO must expose:

- Its depth,
- Its full status, and
- An empty status.

If software writes to this FIFO while it is full, the write must be discarded and an overflow interrupt must be asserted.

### 9.2 Available SETUP Buffer FIFO

Software writes buffer IDs into this FIFO to provide buffers for incoming SETUP packets.

The FIFO must expose:

- Its depth,
- Its full status, and
- An empty status.

If software writes to this FIFO while it is full, the write must be discarded and an overflow interrupt must be asserted.

### 9.3 Received Packet FIFO

The module must use this FIFO to report successfully received OUT and SETUP packets to software.

Each received-packet entry must contain:

- The buffer ID into which the packet was written,
- The received data length in bytes,
- The endpoint number, and
- An indication of whether the packet was a SETUP or an OUT packet.

Software pops an entry by reading the received-packet FIFO. The FIFO must expose:

- Its depth,
- Its empty status, and
- Its full status.

The packet-received interrupt must be asserted while the received-packet FIFO contains at least one entry. It must be a status-type interrupt and must remain asserted until the FIFO is emptied.

### 9.4 FIFO Reset

Software must be able to reset each FIFO independently. Resetting a FIFO must clear all entries and return it to the empty state.

---

## 10. OUT Transaction Behavior

The module must support OUT transactions on enabled endpoints.

For each endpoint, software can configure:

- Whether the endpoint is enabled in the OUT direction.
- Whether OUT packets are enabled for reception.
- Whether SETUP packets are enabled for reception.
- Whether the endpoint is Isochronous.
- Whether the endpoint is stalled.
- Whether the OUT enable bit should be cleared automatically after a received OUT packet.

### 10.1 Endpoint Enable and Flow Control

If an endpoint is not enabled in the OUT direction, the module must ignore OUT tokens directed to that endpoint.

If an endpoint is enabled but OUT reception is not enabled, the module must respond to OUT tokens with a NAK, except for Isochronous endpoints, which do not use NAK handshakes.

### 10.2 Successful OUT Reception

When an OUT packet is accepted:

- A buffer ID must be consumed from the Available OUT Buffer FIFO.
- The packet data must be written into the buffer.
- The received data length, endpoint number, and OUT indication must be pushed into the Received Packet FIFO.
- For non-Isochronous endpoints, an ACK handshake must be returned.
- For Isochronous endpoints, no handshake must be returned.

The recorded data length must exclude the packet CRC. If the CRC bytes fit within the buffer, they may be written after the data but must not be included in the recorded length.

An accepted OUT packet may have a data length of zero. A zero-length packet must be reported with length zero.

### 10.3 Buffer Availability and Backpressure

If no buffer is available in the Available OUT Buffer FIFO:

- Non-Isochronous OUT packets must be NAKed.
- Isochronous OUT packets must be dropped without a handshake.

If the Received Packet FIFO is full or nearly full:

- Non-Isochronous OUT packets must be NAKed.
- Isochronous OUT packets must be dropped without a handshake.

To guarantee that SETUP packets can still be received, regular OUT packets must not be allowed to consume the final available Received Packet FIFO entry. SETUP packets must be permitted to use that final entry.

### 10.4 Data Toggle Handling for OUT

For non-Isochronous endpoints, the module must maintain a data toggle bit per endpoint.

If an OUT packet is received with the expected data toggle, the packet must be accepted and the toggle must be updated.

If an OUT packet is received with the incorrect data toggle, the module must acknowledge the packet and drop it internally. This dropped packet must not be written to the packet buffer and must not be reported in the Received Packet FIFO. This behavior is required by the USB protocol to recover from lost acknowledgments.

### 10.5 Automatic NAK After OUT

If software has set the automatic-NAK-after-OUT option for an endpoint, the module must clear that endpoint’s OUT reception enable bit after successfully receiving an OUT packet. Subsequent OUT packets to that endpoint must then receive NAK responses until software re-enables OUT reception.

### 10.6 OUT STALL

If a non-Isochronous endpoint is stalled, the module must respond to OUT tokens with a STALL handshake. STALL must take priority over NAK.

Receiving a SETUP packet on an endpoint must clear the STALL indication for both the IN and OUT directions of that endpoint.

---

## 11. SETUP Transaction Behavior

SETUP transactions are used only on control endpoints.

For each endpoint, software can enable SETUP reception. If SETUP reception is not enabled for an endpoint, the module must ignore SETUP tokens directed to that endpoint.

When a SETUP packet is accepted:

- A buffer ID must be consumed from the Available SETUP Buffer FIFO.
- The packet data must be written into the buffer.
- The received data length, endpoint number, and SETUP indication must be pushed into the Received Packet FIFO.
- An ACK handshake must be returned.

If no buffer is available in the Available SETUP Buffer FIFO, or if the Received Packet FIFO is full, the SETUP packet must be ignored without a handshake. The host will retry the transaction.

The module must ensure that a SETUP packet can use the final entry of the Received Packet FIFO even when regular OUT packets are being NAKed to keep that entry free.

Receiving a SETUP packet must also:

- Cancel any pending IN transmission on the same endpoint by clearing its ready indication and setting its pending indication.
- Clear the IN and OUT STALL indications for that endpoint.

---

## 12. IN Transaction Behavior

The module must support IN transactions on enabled endpoints.

For each endpoint, software can configure:

- Whether the endpoint is enabled in the IN direction.
- Whether the endpoint is Isochronous.
- Whether the endpoint is stalled.
- The buffer ID and data length of the packet to send.
- Whether the packet is ready to send.

### 12.1 Queuing IN Data

To send data, software writes the buffer ID and data length and sets the ready bit for the endpoint.

If the configured data length is zero, the module must send a CRC-only packet.

If the configured data length is greater than 64 bytes, the module must send only the first 64 bytes.

### 12.2 IN Token Handling

When an IN token is received on an enabled endpoint:

- If the endpoint is stalled and non-Isochronous, the module must respond with a STALL handshake.
- If the endpoint is not stalled and has a packet ready, the module must transmit the packet from the configured buffer.
- If the endpoint is not stalled and no packet is ready:
  - For non-Isochronous endpoints, the module must respond with a NAK.
  - For Isochronous endpoints, the event must be counted as a no-data event and no NAK may be sent.

### 12.3 Successful IN Completion

For non-Isochronous IN endpoints, the transaction completes successfully when the host returns an ACK handshake.

For Isochronous IN endpoints, no handshake is expected. The transaction completes when the packet has been transmitted.

On successful completion:

- The ready bit for the endpoint must be cleared.
- The send-complete indication for the endpoint must be set.
- The packet-sent interrupt must be asserted.

The packet-sent interrupt must remain asserted until software clears all send-complete indications.

If the host responds with a NAK or does not respond, the ready bit must remain set so that the packet can be retried by the host.

### 12.4 Pending and Sending Status

The module must provide status bits for each IN endpoint:

- A ready bit, indicating that software has queued a packet.
- A pending bit, indicating that a queued packet was canceled by hardware due to a link reset or a received SETUP packet.
- A sending bit, indicating that the host has begun collecting the packet.

The sending bit must be set when the first IN token is received while the ready bit is set. It must be cleared on successful completion, on link reset, or when a SETUP packet cancels the transaction.

When a link reset occurs, the module must clear the ready bit for all endpoints and set the pending bit for every endpoint whose ready bit was set.

When a SETUP packet is received on an endpoint, the module must clear the ready bit and set the pending bit for that endpoint.

---

## 13. Data Toggle Control

The module must maintain separate data toggle state for each endpoint in each direction.

Software must be able to:

- Read the current data toggle state for all IN endpoints.
- Read the current data toggle state for all OUT endpoints.
- Update selected endpoint toggles by writing a status value together with a mask.

Masked-off endpoints must remain unchanged when a toggle update is performed.

Data toggles must behave according to the USB protocol for Control, Bulk, and Interrupt endpoints.

---

## 14. Device Address

The module must use a software-programmed device address for matching incoming non-SETUP tokens.

The device address must be cleared to zero by hardware when a link reset occurs.

Software is responsible for programming the address received during a Set Address control transfer after the status stage completes.

---

## 15. Error Handling

The module must detect and report USB protocol errors without corrupting software-visible state.

### 15.1 Packet Errors

The module must detect:

- CRC errors in token packets.
- CRC errors in data packets.
- Invalid packet identifiers.
- Bit-stuffing errors.

Packets with any of these errors must not be transferred to the Received Packet FIFO and must not be reported as successfully received.

The module must assert the appropriate interrupt for each error class.

### 15.2 IN Transaction Errors

The module must raise an IN error interrupt when an IN transaction was attempted but did not complete successfully. This includes:

- The expected ACK handshake was not received.
- The handshake received was invalid.
- The transaction was aborted by another token.

This condition must not clear the ready bit, because the packet should be retried.

### 15.3 OUT Transaction Errors

The module must raise an OUT error interrupt when an OUT transaction was attempted but was dropped. This includes:

- Data toggle mismatch that causes an internal drop.
- Missing Available OUT Buffer FIFO entry.
- Received Packet FIFO full condition.
- Packet or CRC errors.

---

## 16. Interrupts

The module must provide the following interrupts:

| Interrupt | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Packet received | Status-type. Asserted while the Received Packet FIFO is non-empty. |
| Packet sent | Status-type. Asserted while any IN send-complete indication is pending. |
| Disconnected | Event. Asserted when the link enters the disconnected state. |
| Powered | Event. Asserted when the link enters the powered state. |
| Host lost | Event. Asserted when an active link misses SOF for 4.096 ms. |
| Link reset | Event. Asserted when SE0 is detected for approximately 3 µs. |
| Link suspend | Event. Asserted when the link is idle for more than 3 ms. |
| Link resume | Event. Asserted when the link resumes from suspend. |
| Available OUT FIFO empty | Status-type. Asserted while the Available OUT Buffer FIFO is empty and the interface is enabled. |
| Available SETUP FIFO empty | Status-type. Asserted while the Available SETUP Buffer FIFO is empty and the interface is enabled. |
| RX FIFO full | Status-type. Asserted while the Received Packet FIFO is full and the interface is enabled. |
| Available buffer overflow | Event. Asserted when software writes to a full Available Buffer FIFO. |
| IN link error | Event. Asserted when an IN transaction fails. |
| OUT link error | Event. Asserted when an OUT transaction is dropped. |
| RX CRC error | Event. Asserted when a CRC error is detected on a received packet. |
| RX PID error | Event. Asserted when an invalid packet identifier is received. |
| RX bit-stuff error | Event. Asserted when illegal bit stuffing is received. |
| Frame | Event. Asserted when the current frame number changes. |

Software must be able to:

- Read interrupt state.
- Enable or disable each interrupt.
- Force each interrupt through a test bit.
- Clear event-type interrupts by writing 1 to the corresponding state bit.

Status-type interrupts must be cleared by removing the underlying condition.

---

## 17. Start-of-Frame Reference

When reference generation is enabled, the module shall generate a reference pulse when an SOF packet is detected with a valid PID.

The module must also generate a reference-valid output. This output must:

- Assert after the first SOF pulse has been generated.
- Remain asserted while SOF pulses continue to be received and the link is active.
- Deassert if the link becomes inactive.
- Deassert if the host-lost condition occurs.
- Deassert if software disables reference generation.

When software disables reference generation, both the SOF pulse output and the reference-valid output must be forced low.

---

## 18. Suspend and Low-Power Wake Signaling

When the link suspends, the module must stop normal packet processing and deassert the differential receiver enable.

The module must provide a suspend-request output. This output must be pulsed when software writes a 1 to the suspend-request control.

The module must provide a wake-acknowledge output. This output must be pulsed when software writes a 1 to the wake-acknowledge control.

The module must capture low-power wake-monitor status into readable registers. These status fields must reflect the current state of the always-on wake inputs, including:

- Whether the wake monitor is active.
- Whether the bus is non-idle.
- Whether a bus reset was detected by the wake monitor.
- Whether VBUS disconnection was detected by the wake monitor.

The module must also support a resume-link-active control. When software writes this control, and the link is in the powered state, the module must enter the resuming state. This allows the link to return to active operation after the module has been powered down.

---

## 19. Alerts

The module must report a fatal alert if a bus integrity error is detected.

Software must be able to trigger a test alert through the alert test register.

---

## 20. Diagnostic Counters

The module must provide diagnostic counters for exceptional USB events.

The following OUT-side events must be countable:

- SETUP packets ignored because no SETUP buffer was available.
- OUT packets dropped because no OUT buffer was available.
- SETUP/OUT packets dropped because the Received Packet FIFO was full.
- OUT packets acknowledged and dropped due to data toggle mismatch.

The following IN-side events must be countable:

- IN transactions that timed out waiting for a handshake.
- IN transactions that received a NAK handshake.
- IN transactions attempted when no packet data was available.

A second no-data counter must also be available so that software can partition endpoint monitoring between counters.

The following error events must be countable:

- CRC5 errors on token packets.
- CRC16 errors on data packets.
- Bit-stuffing errors.
- Invalid packet identifiers.

Each counter must:

- Count only events explicitly enabled by software.
- Count only events on endpoints selected by software, where endpoint association is meaningful.
- Provide a readable count value.
- Be resettable by software.

The counters must not alter USB behavior; they provide visibility only.

---

## 21. Register and Status Visibility

The module must expose the following status information to software:

- Current link state.
- Current frame number, taken from a fully valid SOF when available and otherwise advanced by SOF timing events.
- Host-lost condition.
- VBUS sense state.
- Available OUT Buffer FIFO depth.
- Available SETUP Buffer FIFO depth.
- Received Packet FIFO depth.
- FIFO empty and full status.
- Current data toggle states.
- Current PHY input and output states.
- Low-power wake-monitor states.

Software must be able to configure:

- USB interface enable.
- Device address.
- Endpoint enables.
- SETUP and OUT reception enables.
- Automatic NAK-after-OUT behavior.
- IN packet configuration for each endpoint.
- STALL behavior.
- Isochronous endpoint configuration.
- Data toggle updates.
- PHY configuration.
- PHY output override.
- FIFO resets.
- Interrupt enables.
- Alert test.
- Diagnostic counter enables and resets.

---

## 22. Interface Enable and Initialization

The module must not assert any USB pullup until software explicitly enables the interface.

Endpoint 0 should be enabled in both the IN and OUT directions before the interface is enabled.

When the interface is enabled and VBUS is present, the module must perform device attachment by asserting the Full-Speed pullup.

After attachment, the module must wait for a link reset from the host before normal packet traffic is processed.

---

## 23. Behavior When the Link Is Suspended

While the link is suspended:

- The module must not respond to USB transactions.
- The differential receiver must be disabled if it is controlled by the module.
- Software must be able to read the suspended state and receive the link-suspend interrupt.

When resume signaling is detected, the module must generate a link-resume interrupt and transition back toward the active state.

---

## 24. Behavior on Link Reset

When a link reset is detected:

- The module must generate a link-reset interrupt.
- The programmed device address must be cleared.
- All pending IN ready bits must be cleared.
- Pending bits for canceled IN packets must be set.
- STALL flags must be cleared for endpoints that receive a subsequent SETUP packet.

After the reset ends, the link must enter the active-no-SOF state and wait for a start-of-frame packet.

---

## 25. Behavior When VBUS Is Lost

If VBUS is lost:

- The module must deassert the Full-Speed pullup.
- The link must enter the disconnected state.
- A disconnected interrupt must be generated.
- The module must not respond to USB traffic until VBUS returns and software re-enables the interface if required.

---

## 26. Isochronous Behavior

The module must support Isochronous OUT and IN endpoints up to a maximum packet size of 64 bytes.

For Isochronous OUT transactions:

- No handshake is returned.
- If a buffer is available and the Received Packet FIFO has space, the packet is accepted and reported.
- If no buffer is available or the Received Packet FIFO is full, the packet is dropped.

For Isochronous IN transactions:

- No handshake is expected.
- If a packet is ready, it is transmitted and counted as sent.
- If no packet is ready, the transaction is counted as a no-data event.

Isochronous endpoints must not use data toggle tracking.

---

## 27. Transaction Retry Behavior

The module must not silently retry failed non-Isochronous transactions by itself. Instead:

- If a packet is not acknowledged, the module leaves the packet ready so that the host may retry the transaction.
- If the module NAKs an OUT or IN transaction, the host is expected to retry later.
- If a SETUP packet cannot be accepted, no handshake is returned and the host must retry.

The module must provide interrupt visibility for repeated exceptional conditions to allow software to diagnose bus performance or signal-integrity issues.

---

## 28. Reset and Power-Up Defaults

At power-up and after reset:

- The USB interface must be disabled.
- No pullup may be asserted.
- All endpoints must be disabled.
- All FIFOs must be empty.
- No packets may be queued for transmission.
- All STALL bits must be cleared.
- Data toggles must be cleared.
- Device address must be zero.
- All interrupts and alerts must be deasserted.
- The link state must be reported as disconnected.

---

## 29. Summary of Key Constraints

- The module must operate as a USB 2.0 Full-Speed device.
- It must support packet sizes up to 64 bytes.
- It must support up to 12 endpoints.
- It must provide a 2 KiB packet buffer.
- It must support Control, Bulk, Interrupt, and Isochronous transactions.
- It must maintain separate IN and OUT data toggles.
- It must report all link state changes and packet events through interrupts.
- It must provide a clock-reference output based on received SOF packets.
- It must support suspend, resume, and low-power wake signaling.
- It must provide comprehensive software-visible status and diagnostic counters.

# Behavioral Specification: USB Link State Monitor

## Overview

This module monitors the state of a Full-Speed USB device link and reports the current link state and link events. It combines information about VBUS presence, the state of the D+/D- lines, bus activity, and start-of-frame reception to determine whether the link is disconnected, powered, active, suspended, resuming, or being reset.

The module operates from a 48 MHz clock and uses a microsecond timebase for its timeout measurements. All outputs change synchronously with the 48 MHz clock.

## Reset and Initialization

After reset, the module shall:

- Report the link as **Disconnected**.
- Deassert all event outputs except the disconnect indication.
- Clear all timers and counters.
- Be ready to detect VBUS presence as soon as the power-sense input is debounced.

## Input Qualification

### Power Sense

The VBUS presence input shall be debounced so that short glitches do not cause link state changes. The module shall use the debounced value for all power-related decisions. A power-present indication shall be asserted only after the raw VBUS sense has been stable for the debounce period.

### SE0 Detection

A single-ended zero (SE0) condition shall be detected only when both D+ and D- are low. The module shall ignore the line state while the device itself is driving the bus; in other words, an SE0 shall be recognized only when the transmit output enable is inactive.

The SE0 condition shall also be debounced so that brief line glitches do not trigger reset detection. Short SE0 pulses shorter than the debounce period shall be ignored.

## Link States

The module shall maintain exactly one of the following link states:

| Value | State | Description |
|------:|-------|-------------|
| 0 | Disconnected | VBUS is absent, or the pull-up is disabled. |
| 1 | Powered | VBUS is present, the pull-up is enabled, but the link has not been reset. |
| 2 | Powered Suspended | VBUS is present, the link has not been reset, and the bus has been idle for more than 3 ms. |
| 3 | Active | The link has been reset and is operating normally, including having received at least one SOF. |
| 4 | Suspended | The link was active and has been idle for more than 3 ms. |
| 5 | Active No SOF | The link has been reset and is active, but no SOF has yet been received. |
| 6 | Resuming | Resume signaling is in progress, but the end of resume signaling has not yet been detected. |

## State Transition Requirements

The module shall implement the following behavior:

### Disconnected

The link shall be in the Disconnected state after reset, whenever VBUS is absent, or whenever the pull-up enable is deasserted.

When VBUS is present and the pull-up is enabled, the module shall transition from Disconnected to Powered.

A loss of VBUS or removal of the pull-up enable shall take priority over all other state transitions and shall force the link into Disconnected from any state.

### Powered

While in Powered, the module shall:

- Transition to **Active No SOF** when a valid bus reset completes.
- Transition to **Resuming** when a software-directed resume request is asserted.
- Transition to **Powered Suspended** when the bus has been idle for more than 3 ms.

A valid reset shall take priority over the other transitions.

### Powered Suspended

While in Powered Suspended, the module shall:

- Transition to **Active No SOF** when a valid bus reset completes.
- Transition to **Powered** and assert the resume output when bus activity is detected.

### Resuming

While in Resuming, the module is waiting for the end of resume signaling.

The module shall transition to **Active No SOF** and assert the resume output when either:

- A valid bus reset completes, or
- The J (idle) state is detected, indicating the end of resume signaling.

### Active No SOF

While in Active No SOF, the module shall:

- Transition to **Active** when an SOF is received.
- Transition to **Suspended** when the bus has been idle for more than 3 ms.
- Remain in Active No SOF if a bus reset occurs; the reset condition shall still be reported and shall clear SOF-monitoring state.

### Active

While in Active, the module shall:

- Transition to **Suspended** when the bus has been idle for more than 3 ms.
- Transition to **Active No SOF** when a valid bus reset completes.

### Suspended

While in Suspended, the module shall:

- Transition to **Resuming** when bus activity is detected.
- Transition to **Active No SOF** and assert the resume output when a valid bus reset completes.

## Event Outputs

### Disconnect Output

The disconnect output shall be asserted whenever the link state is Disconnected. This includes the case where VBUS is absent and the case where the pull-up is disabled.

### Powered Output

The powered output shall be asserted whenever the debounced VBUS-present indication is true. It is independent of the pull-up enable and may be asserted even while the link state is Disconnected.

### Active Output

The active output shall be asserted whenever the link state is either **Active** or **Active No SOF**.

### Suspend Output

The suspend output shall be asserted whenever the link state is either **Suspended** or **Powered Suspended**.

### Reset Output

The reset output shall be asserted when a valid reset condition has been recognized. A valid reset requires a debounced SE0 condition to persist for at least 3 microseconds.

The reset output shall remain asserted until the SE0 condition is removed. A shorter SE0 pulse shall not cause the reset output to assert.

### Resume Output

The resume output shall be asserted as a pulse when the link leaves a suspended condition and becomes active again. Specifically, the module shall assert the resume output when:

- A Powered Suspended link detects bus activity.
- A Resuming link detects the end of resume signaling or a bus reset.
- A Suspended link detects a bus reset.

A reset that occurs before the link has ever become active shall not generate a resume pulse.

## SOF Monitoring and Host Loss

The module shall monitor SOF reception while the link is active.

### SOF Missed

If no SOF is received within 1.005 ms while the link is active, the module shall assert a SOF-missed output pulse.

If no SOF arrives, this pulse shall be generated again each 1.005 ms until an SOF is received, the link stops being active, or a reset is detected.

The SOF-missed timer shall be cleared by:

- Reception of an SOF.
- The link becoming inactive.
- Detection of a reset.

### Host Lost

The module shall assert the host-lost output after four consecutive SOF-missed events occur while the link is active.

The host-lost output shall remain asserted until one of the following occurs:

- An SOF is received.
- The link becomes inactive.
- A reset is detected.

While the link is not active, SOF-missed and host-lost outputs shall not be asserted.

## Link State Output

The module shall provide a 3-bit link state output that reflects the current state using the encodings listed in the Link States table.

The output shall be updated whenever the link state changes.

# Behavioral Specification for `usbdev_usbif`

## 1. Overview

This module provides the core USB 2.0 Full-Speed device interface functionality. It operates on the 48 MHz USB clock and integrates the low-level USB protocol handling, link-state monitoring, packet buffer arbitration, and endpoint transaction control.

The module shall:

- Support a compile-time-configurable number of endpoints, up to 16 and typically 12.
- Support Full-Speed USB packet sizes up to 64 bytes.
- Support SETUP, OUT, and IN transactions.
- Support Bulk, Control, Interrupt, and Isochronous endpoint behavior.
- Provide the USB-side interface to a shared packet buffer used for received and transmitted packet data.
- Report link state, frame timing, protocol errors, and transaction events to the rest of the system.

---

## 2. Reset and Initialization

After reset, the module shall:

- Assume the disconnected link state.
- Clear the current frame number to zero.
- Not assert the USB pull-up.
- Not drive the USB lines actively.

The module shall be held in reset while the reset input is asserted and shall become operational synchronously with the 48 MHz clock after reset is released.

---

## 3. USB Connection and Pull-Up Control

The module shall assert the USB Full-Speed D+ pull-up only when both of the following conditions are true:

- The interface is enabled by software.
- Valid USB host VBUS is sensed.

If either condition becomes false, the pull-up shall be deasserted, causing the device to appear disconnected from the USB bus.

The module shall also generate a device-address clear indication whenever the interface is disabled or a USB link reset is detected. This ensures that a previously assigned USB device address is cleared on disconnect and reset.

---

## 4. USB Physical Interface

The module shall drive and receive the USB D+/D− signals according to the configured PHY mode.

The module shall support:

- Two transmit encodings:
  1. Direct D+ and D− data outputs.
  2. A data output plus a separate single-ended-zero (SE0) output.
- Two receive modes:
  1. Recovery of the differential K/J symbols from an external differential receiver output.
  2. Recovery of K/J symbols directly from the single-ended D+ and D− inputs.
- Flipping of the D+ and D− signals.
- Recognition of a single SE0 bit as an end-of-packet, as an alternative to requiring two SE0 bits.

In oscillator test mode, the module shall continuously transmit a repeating J/K pattern on the USB outputs. While in this mode, it shall not require valid start-of-frame reception.

---

## 5. Receive Path: OUT and SETUP Transactions

### 5.1 General Receive Behavior

For an OUT or SETUP packet directed at an enabled endpoint, the module shall determine whether the packet can be accepted based on:

- Whether the endpoint is enabled.
- Whether the endpoint is stalled.
- Whether the endpoint has receive flow-control enabled.
- Whether an available buffer is present in the appropriate Available Buffer FIFO.
- Whether the Received Buffer FIFO can accept the completed packet record.

### 5.2 Endpoint Enable and Disable

- If the endpoint is disabled for OUT or SETUP reception, the packet shall be ignored.
- If the endpoint is enabled and configured to accept SETUP packets, SETUP packets shall be accepted according to the buffer availability rules below.
- If the endpoint is enabled for OUT reception, OUT packets shall be accepted, NAKed, or dropped according to flow-control and buffer availability.

### 5.3 Stall Behavior

For non-isochronous endpoints, if the endpoint is configured to STALL, the module shall cause a STALL handshake to be returned for OUT transactions. STALL shall take priority over NAK and buffer-based flow control.

For endpoints configured to accept SETUP packets, a SETUP packet shall not be stalled. Instead, it shall be accepted if possible or ignored if no buffer is available.

### 5.4 Buffer and FIFO Flow Control

The module shall maintain separate available-buffer paths for SETUP and OUT packets.

- A SETUP packet must be accepted whenever an Available SETUP Buffer is present, even if the Received Buffer FIFO is otherwise full.
- An OUT packet shall be NAKed (for non-isochronous endpoints) or ignored (for isochronous endpoints) if no Available OUT Buffer is present.
- An OUT packet shall also be NAKed or ignored if the Received Buffer FIFO cannot accept a completion record.
- A SETUP packet shall be ignored only when no Available SETUP Buffer is present.

This reserved treatment of SETUP packets ensures that control transfers can still be received under heavy OUT traffic or high software latency.

### 5.5 Packet Write and Completion

When an OUT or SETUP packet is accepted, the module shall:

- Take the next buffer ID from the appropriate Available Buffer FIFO.
- Write the received packet payload into the packet buffer at the selected buffer.
- Append the received CRC bytes to the buffer only if they fit within the buffer capacity.
- Exclude the CRC bytes from the reported packet size.
- Generate a completion record containing:
  - The endpoint number.
  - Whether the packet was a SETUP or OUT packet.
  - The payload byte count.
  - The buffer ID used.
- Make the completion record available to the Received Buffer FIFO.
- Consume the Available Buffer FIFO entry only when the packet is successfully accepted.

The module shall also generate a dedicated SETUP-received indication as part of the completion of each accepted SETUP packet. This indication allows the rest of the system to cancel any pending IN transmission on the same control endpoint.

### 5.6 Endpoint Number Validity

When reporting the endpoint number for a received packet, the module shall only indicate that the endpoint number is valid when it is within the configured endpoint range. If the incoming transaction refers to an out-of-range endpoint, the reported endpoint number shall be forced to a safe value and the valid indication shall be deasserted.

---

## 6. Transmit Path: IN Transactions

### 6.1 Data Transmission

When the host issues an IN transaction to an enabled IN endpoint, the module shall:

- Use the configured buffer ID and byte count for that endpoint.
- Read the packet data from the packet buffer in sequential byte order starting at offset zero.
- Transmit the configured number of bytes.
- Support a zero-byte packet, transmitting a CRC-only packet.

If the configured byte count is larger than the maximum packet size, the module shall transmit only the maximum packet size.

### 6.2 Endpoint Not Ready

If the endpoint is enabled but no data is marked ready, the module shall cause a NAK handshake to be returned for the IN transaction, except for isochronous endpoints where the transaction is completed without a handshake.

### 6.3 Stall Behavior

For non-isochronous endpoints, if the endpoint is configured to STALL, the module shall cause a STALL handshake to be returned for IN transactions. STALL shall take priority over NAK.

### 6.4 Isochronous Behavior

For isochronous IN endpoints, the module shall transmit the data packet without expecting an ACK handshake from the host.

### 6.5 Transaction Indications

The module shall provide indications when an IN transaction starts and when it ends. These indications shall identify the endpoint involved and shall be generated regardless of whether the transaction completed with ACK, NAK, STALL, or error, as appropriate.

The module shall also generate an endpoint-valid indication for the IN endpoint so that out-of-range endpoint numbers are not used to index endpoint arrays.

### 6.6 Effect of SETUP Reception

If a SETUP packet is accepted on a control endpoint, the module shall emit the SETUP-received indication. This indication is the mechanism by which any pending IN transaction on that endpoint is canceled, allowing the endpoint to be used for the control transfer.

---

## 7. Packet Buffer Interface

The module shall be responsible for all USB-side accesses to the packet buffer.

### 7.1 Receive Writes

Received packet data shall be packed into 32-bit words before being written to the packet buffer. The module shall write only the words that contain received payload bytes. For the final partial word, a write shall be performed if at least one payload byte is present.

The buffer address shall be derived from the selected buffer ID and the current byte offset within the packet. The module shall not write beyond the buffer capacity. The two CRC bytes may be stored after the payload if they fit, but they shall not be included in the reported packet size.

### 7.2 Transmit Reads

For IN transactions, the module shall read the packet data from the packet buffer in byte order. A read of the first word of the packet shall be initiated when the packet starts, and subsequent reads shall occur as the transmit engine consumes data.

The module shall continue reading until the configured packet size is reached.

---

## 8. Start-of-Frame and Frame Number Handling

The module shall detect valid Start-of-Frame (SOF) packets generated by the host.

On each valid SOF, the module shall:

- Capture the frame index from the SOF packet.
- Update the current frame number to the received value.
- Generate a frame-start indication whenever the frame number changes.

If the link is active but SOF packets stop being received, the module shall:

- Continue to advance the frame number at the nominal 1 ms rate using an internal timer.
- Generate frame-start indications for these internally generated frame updates.
- Assert a host-lost indication after the expected SOF interval is missed by a significant margin, nominally 4.096 ms.

This behavior preserves a local frame reference even when the host SOF stream is interrupted.

---

## 9. Link State Monitoring

The module shall continuously monitor the state of the USB lines and VBUS sense, and shall report the current link state.

The reported link states shall include:

- Disconnected.
- Powered.
- Powered and suspended.
- Active with no SOF received yet.
- Active.
- Suspended.
- Resuming.

The module shall generate individual status indications for the following link events:

- Disconnect: loss of VBUS or removal of the pull-up.
- Power: VBUS present and pull-up applied.
- Reset: sustained SE0 on the USB lines, nominally for 3 µs.
- Suspend: idle J state on the USB lines for more than 3 ms.
- Resume: non-idle signaling after a suspended state.
- Active: normal operation after reset.
- Host lost: active link without received SOF packets for the required timeout.

A link reset indication shall also cause the device-address clear indication to be asserted, so the host-assigned address is discarded.

---

## 10. Data Toggle Management

The module shall maintain data toggle state for each IN and OUT endpoint.

The module shall:

- Update OUT endpoint data toggles after accepted OUT transactions.
- Update IN endpoint data toggles after successfully acknowledged IN transactions.
- Expose the current data toggle state for software readback.
- Accept masked software writes to modify selected endpoint data toggles without affecting others.

For endpoints configured as control endpoints, SETUP transactions shall reset the associated data toggle behavior according to the USB protocol.

---

## 11. Protocol Error Reporting

The module shall report the following error conditions on received packets:

- CRC5 errors on token packets.
- CRC16 errors on received data packets.
- Invalid packet identifiers (PIDs).
- Bit-stuffing violations.

These error indications shall be provided as individual status outputs.

Invalid packets shall not be committed to the Received Buffer FIFO and shall not produce a successful receive completion.

---

## 12. Transaction Event Indications

The module shall provide event indications for the following transaction-level conditions:

- A SETUP packet ignored because no Available SETUP Buffer was present.
- An OUT packet ignored or NAKed because no Available OUT Buffer was present.
- A SETUP or OUT packet dropped or NAKed because the Received Buffer FIFO was not ready.
- An OUT transaction with an incorrect data toggle that was accepted and dropped internally.
- An IN transaction that timed out because no handshake was received from the host.
- An IN transaction that was NAKed.
- An IN transaction attempted when no packet data was available.

These event indications are provided for use by event counters and should reflect the behavior of each corresponding transaction.

---

## 13. Configuration and Endpoint Controls

The module shall accept configuration inputs that control endpoint behavior. These include:

- Per-endpoint OUT and IN enable.
- Per-endpoint SETUP and OUT receive enable.
- Per-endpoint STALL configuration.
- Per-endpoint isochronous mode selection.
- Per-endpoint IN buffer ID, size, and ready indication.
- Per-endpoint data toggle initial state and masked updates.

The module shall implement the following priority rules:

- A STALL configuration shall take priority over NAK and flow-control-based responses for non-isochronous endpoints.
- An endpoint with SETUP receive enabled shall be treated as a control endpoint. For control endpoints, the isochronous configuration shall be ignored.
- A disabled endpoint shall not participate in USB transactions.

---

## 14. Parameterization and Constraints

The module shall be parameterizable for the number of endpoints, available-buffer FIFO widths, received-buffer FIFO width, maximum packet size, number of buffers, and packet buffer address width.

The design shall enforce the following parameter constraints:

- The number of endpoints shall be greater than zero and no greater than 16.
- The maximum packet size shall be 64 bytes.
- The number of buffers shall be greater than one.
- The packet buffer address width shall be sufficient to address all configured buffers.

These constraints shall be checked as part of design elaboration so that invalid configurations are rejected.

---

## 15. Summary of Key Behaviors

In summary, the module shall:

- Present a USB Full-Speed device to the host when enabled and powered.
- Receive OUT and SETUP packets into software-provided buffers, giving SETUP packets priority.
- Transmit IN packets from software-provided buffers in response to host IN tokens.
- Maintain frame timing and link state.
- Track data toggles.
- Report protocol errors and transaction events.
- Provide safe endpoint indices and valid indications to prevent out-of-bounds accesses.
